notes:
This release includes everything from 2.0.0-beta.69 to 2.0.0-beta.73.

Customer statements and payments

Statement of account for a period (now the default kind of statement): the balance brought forward, then every invoice (paid or open), payment (with the invoices it paid), credit memo, journal and sales receipt in the period, with a running balance; the balance at the end and its ageing. Read from QuickBooks for the customer and its jobs. Choose the period on the Statements page or the customer’s page, and the e-mail subject names it. The statement of open invoices is still available.
Statements list: now shows every customer, so someone who owes nothing can be sent a statement of their payments.
A/R account on Record payment: with more than one Accounts Receivable account, choose it beside the customer, as in QuickBooks’ Receive Payments. Only that account’s invoices are shown, and the payment (or prepayment) goes to it in QuickBooks. It starts as the account last used for the customer.
Customer changes save at once: Edit details… and Set type… no longer wait for QuickBooks. The change goes to QuickBooks in the background, and the customer’s page shows when QuickBooks has it.
Member ID: the customer’s Account No. in QuickBooks is shown as Member ID and can be changed under Edit details….

Insurance EOBs

Patients by member ID: the EOB’s member ID is matched to the customer’s Member ID first, then by name. This settles two patients with the same name.
Other insurers’ EOBs: an EOB in a layout the app doesn’t know asks once Which column is which? It is remembered for that insurer, and Change the columns… shows it again.
Reports → Insurance claims outstanding: open invoices with a claim number (the P.O. No. on the invoice), by insurer (the patient’s customer type) and age (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, over 90 days), with an Excel (CSV) export.

Reconcile helper and bank statements

Matched groups as one row: a group of several lines shows its totals, and ▸ Show opens it. The CSV export works the same way.
“Group these” on a bank rule: the rule’s lines are suggested together, first, against the one QuickBooks entry they add up to (e.g. the month’s service charges and GCT entered as one cheque).
Split across payees: one bank debit that paid several vendors becomes a payment voucher for each, with its own GL account. References get -1, -2 and so on, and all the vouchers are linked to the bank line.
Teach a layout (Banking → Statement layouts): for a bank or card statement PDF the app doesn’t read, click its column headings and balance labels once. It is saved only when the statement adds up, then used for that bank’s statements from then on. Layouts can be exported and imported as .swit-layout files to share between clients.

Everywhere

Slow saves say why: when a Save takes more than 2 seconds, a note at the bottom of the screen shows what it is waiting for, either files uploading or the QuickBooks job running.

New settings: the statement made by default, and the statement of account’s opening line.
